correctness.rationale: In a binary cube a total mutual-visibility set is exactly a set with no distance-2 pair: a distance-2 selected pair blocks both length-2 paths between their two common neighbors, while if none exists a shortest path can greedily avoid selected internal vertices. The parity halves of Q7 are independent copies of the 64-vertex halved cube H with edges at Hamming distance 2; maximal visibility means independent domination in BOTH halves. In H a closed neighborhood has 22 vertices; independent centers distance 4 have intersection size 6, distance 6 disjoint, with triple distance-4 intersection size 1. Three independent neighborhoods cover <64; four dominate iff exactly two disjoint distance-6 pairs, giving union size 64. Fix one center, choose its distance-6 partner in 7 ways and a complementary 3+3 partition in 10 ways; gives 64*70/4=1120 quadruples per parity, hence gamma_lower=8 and 1120^2=1,254,400 labeled achievers. Independent exhaustive enumeration of all parity independent dominating 4-sets gave precisely 1120, 70 through zero. The known maximum 16 is separately supported by a length-7 simplex code and elementary distance bound, not an unproved inference from the minimum.

value.rationale: Determines a naturally posed lower total-visibility invariant for the first nontrivial seven-dimensional cube and exactly describes and counts every extremizer. Relates the independence complex facets to binary code geometry and proves nonpurity with a sharp eight-versus-sixteen witness, a useful finite classification.
